questions.question: Hughston's posteromedial drawer sign is performed with the patient supine, knee flexed 80-90°, hip flexed 45°, and the foot slightly medially rotated. A positive test (excessive posterior movement/rotation of the medial tibia) is most indicative of injury to which primary structure?

options.B: Posterior cruciate ligament (along with posteromedial supporting structures)

questions.explanation: A positive Hughston's posteromedial drawer sign indicates injury to the posterior cruciate ligament, along with possible involvement of the posterior oblique ligament, medial collateral ligament, semimembranosus, and posteromedial capsule — it tests for posteromedial rotary instability of the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Ligament Stability, Posteromedial and Posterolateral Drawer Sign

questions.question: The Jakob test (reverse pivot shift maneuver) is used to assess for which type of knee instability?

options.C: Isolated medial collateral ligament sprain only

questions.explanation: The Jakob test (reverse pivot shift maneuver) tests for posterolateral rotary instability — a positive test (jerk in the knee, or posterior tibial shift with a 'giving way' sensation) indicates injury to the lateral collateral ligament, arcuate-popliteus complex, and mid-third of the lateral capsule.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Tests for Posterolateral Rotary Instability

questions.question: The KT-1000 arthrometer is primarily used to measure which type of knee displacement?

options.A: Anteroposterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur

questions.explanation: The KT-1000 arthrometer is the most commonly used ligament testing device for the knee, measuring anteroposterior (forward-backward) displacement of the tibia relative to the femur, used to quantify ligamentous laxity (e.g. in ACL/PCL injury) as an adjunct to clinical assessment.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment

questions.question: Using the KT-1000 arthrometer, a difference of more than 3 mm in anterior displacement between the injured and uninjured knee is generally considered:

options.A: A normal finding requiring no further action
options.B: Diagnostic for injury to the anterior or posterior cruciate ligament
options.C: Evidence of a meniscal tear specifically, never a ligament injury

questions.explanation: A side-to-side difference of more than 3 mm in anterior displacement on KT-1000 arthrometer testing is generally considered diagnostic for injury to the anterior cruciate ligament or posterior cruciate ligament.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment

questions.question: Which two special tests are classically used to assess for a meniscal injury of the knee?

options.B: Lachman test and pivot shift test
options.C: Clarke's sign and the Q-angle measurement
options.D: Noble compression test and Ober's test

questions.explanation: The McMurray test and Apley's (compression/distraction) test are the classic special tests for meniscal injury of the knee, alongside the 'bounce home' test.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Special Tests Commonly Performed on the Knee

questions.question: Why can a meniscal injury sometimes present with little or no pain or swelling, making diagnosis more difficult?

options.A: The menisci are avascular and have no nerve supply on their inner two-thirds
options.B: The menisci are the most richly innervated structures in the knee
options.C: Meniscal tears always occur alongside complete ACL rupture, masking symptoms
options.D: Meniscal tissue regenerates immediately after injury

questions.explanation: The menisci are avascular and lack nerve supply on their inner two-thirds, meaning an injury confined to this region can produce little or no pain or swelling — one reason meniscal injury can be difficult to diagnose confidently without a thorough history and examination.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Tests for Meniscus Injury

questions.question: Which special test is specifically associated with assessing patellofemoral (patellar) instability?
questions.explanation: The apprehension test is used to assess for patellar instability — the examiner laterally displaces the patella and observes for a look or feeling of apprehension from the patient, who fears the patella is about to dislocate.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Special Tests Commonly Performed on the Knee

questions.question: The Noble compression test is used to assess for which condition?
questions.explanation: The Noble compression test is used to assess for iliotibial band friction syndrome, a common cause of lateral knee pain particularly in runners.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Special Tests Commonly Performed on the Knee

questions.question: Clarke's sign and the McConnell test are both special tests associated with which condition?
questions.explanation: Clarke's sign and the McConnell test are both used in the assessment of patellofemoral syndrome (anterior knee pain related to patellar tracking/compression issues).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Special Tests Commonly Performed on the Knee

questions.question: In the tibial external rotation (Dial) test, if the tibia rotates MORE at 90° of knee flexion than at 30°, this pattern most likely indicates injury to:

options.A: Only the popliteus corner (isolated posterolateral injury)
options.B: Both the popliteus corner AND the posterior cruciate ligament
options.C: The anterior cruciate ligament in isolation

questions.explanation: In the Dial test, if the tibia rotates less at 90° than at 30°, an isolated posterolateral (popliteus corner) injury is more likely. If it rotates MORE at 90° than at 30°, combined injury to both the popliteus corner and the posterior cruciate ligament is more likely.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Tibial External Rotation (Dial) Test

questions.question: The External Rotation Recurvatum Test, in which the examiner lifts both of the patient's big toes off the table and observes for relative hyperextension and lateral tibial rotation on the affected side, is a test for:
questions.explanation: The External Rotation Recurvatum Test assesses for posterolateral rotary instability in extension — a positive test shows the affected knee falling into relative hyperextension (genu varum appearance) with lateral tibial rotation due to gravity, when both legs are lifted by the toes.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — External Rotation Recurvatum Test

questions.question: In arthrometer testing, the 'quadriceps active position' refers to the knee angle at which:

options.A: The tibia shows no forward movement when the quadriceps contracts, typically around 70° of flexion
options.B: The knee is fully extended at 0°
options.C: The patient is asked to relax completely with no muscle contraction
options.D: The hamstrings are maximally contracted instead of the quadriceps

questions.explanation: The quadriceps neutral (active) angle is the knee flexion angle — typically around 70° — at which an isolated quadriceps contraction produces no anterior tibial translation in a normal knee; this position is used as a reference when testing the injured knee for abnormal anterior displacement (suggestive of PCL injury).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment

questions.question: The Neer impingement test involves the examiner passively and forcibly elevating the patient's medially-rotated arm in the scapular plane. A positive test (pain) is most indicative of an overuse injury to which structure?

options.A: The supraspinatus muscle (and sometimes the biceps tendon)

questions.explanation: The Neer impingement test causes 'jamming' of the greater tuberosity against the anteroinferior border of the acromion; a positive test (reproducing pain) is indicative of an overuse injury to the supraspinatus muscle, and sometimes the biceps tendon.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Common Shoulder Impingement Tests, Neer Impingement Test

questions.question: The Hawkins-Kennedy impingement test involves forward flexing the arm to 90° and then forcibly:
questions.explanation: In the Hawkins-Kennedy test, the examiner forward flexes the arm to 90° and then forcibly medially rotates the shoulder, pushing the supraspinatus tendon against the coracoacromial ligament and coracoid process — pain indicates a positive test for supraspinatus tendinosis or impingement.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment

questions.question: A 'Bankart lesion' of the shoulder refers to:

options.A: Detachment of the anteroinferior labrum, commonly occurring with traumatic anterior dislocation
options.B: A tear confined strictly to the superior labrum (10 to 2 o'clock position)
options.C: A rotator cuff tear with no labral involvement
options.D: A fracture of the greater tuberosity

questions.explanation: A Bankart lesion is a tear of the anteroinferior labrum (roughly the 3 to 7 o'clock position in the right shoulder), most commonly occurring with a traumatic anterior dislocation, also compromising the stability of the inferior glenohumeral ligament.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Tests for Labral Tears

questions.question: A SLAP lesion (Superior Labrum, Anterior and Posterior) involves detachment of the labrum at approximately which clock-face position, and is often caused by what mechanism?

options.A: 10 to 2 o'clock position; often from a FOOSH injury or during deceleration in throwing
options.B: 3 to 7 o'clock position; only from anterior dislocation
options.C: 6 o'clock position exclusively; from a direct blow to the shoulder
options.D: SLAP lesions never have an identifiable mechanism

questions.explanation: A SLAP lesion involves detachment of the labrum from roughly the 10 to 2 o'clock position, often occurring from a FOOSH (fall on outstretched hand) injury or during the deceleration phase of throwing; if the biceps tendon also detaches, the superior glenohumeral ligament support is lost and the shoulder becomes unstable.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Tests for Labral Tears

questions.question: Per Snyder's classification, a Type II SLAP lesion — described as the most common type — is characterised by:

options.A: A superior labrum that is markedly frayed but with intact attachments
options.B: A small tear with instability of the labral-biceps complex
options.C: A bucket-handle tear that may displace into the joint, with the labral-biceps attachment intact
options.D: A bucket-handle tear extending to the biceps tendon, allowing it to sublux into the joint

questions.explanation: Snyder's classification describes Type I (frayed superior labrum, intact attachments), Type II (small tear with labral-biceps complex instability — the most common type), Type III (bucket-handle tear, labral-biceps attachment intact), and Type IV (bucket-handle tear extending to the biceps tendon, allowing subluxation).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Tests for Labral Tears, SLAP Classification

questions.question: In the Active Compression Test of O'Brien, pain that is present with the arm pronated (thumb down) but reduced or eliminated with the arm supinated (thumb up) suggests a positive test for:

options.B: A simple rotator cuff strain with no labral involvement

questions.explanation: O'Brien's active compression test is positive for a superior labral injury when pain (felt 'inside' the shoulder, not at the AC joint) is produced with the arm pronated, and is reduced or eliminated when the same maneuver is repeated with the arm supinated.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Active Compression Test of O'Brien

questions.question: Posterior internal impingement of the shoulder, commonly seen in overhead athletes, occurs when the rotator cuff impinges against the posterosuperior edge of the glenoid, with the arm positioned in:

options.C: Complete elbow flexion with the shoulder neutral
options.D: Full flexion with the forearm pronated

questions.explanation: Posterior internal impingement occurs when the arm is abducted, extended, and laterally rotated — a position common in the late cocking phase of throwing — causing the rotator cuff to impinge against the posterosuperior glenoid rim, sometimes producing a 'kissing' labral lesion.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Posterior Internal Impingement Test

questions.question: The earliest and most important clinical sign of impending Volkmann's ischaemic contracture after a supracondylar fracture is:

options.B: Pain on passive extension of the fingers

questions.explanation: Severe, increasing forearm pain aggravated by passive finger extension indicates ischaemia of the deep flexor compartment. Pulse loss is a late sign; claw deformity is the established contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In established Volkmann's ischaemic contracture, the finger deformity is reduced (fingers can be extended) when the wrist is:
questions.explanation: Flexor muscles are shortened; flexing the wrist slackens them and allows the fingers to straighten. With the wrist extended the fingers flex (tenodesis effect).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A Colles' fracture is a fracture of the:

options.B: Distal end of the radius with dorsal displacement

questions.explanation: Colles' fracture: extra-articular fracture of the distal radius (within 2.5 cm of the wrist) with dorsal angulation — the ‘dinner-fork’ deformity. Volar displacement is Smith's fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most common complication after a Colles' fracture is:

options.A: Stiffness of the fingers and wrist

questions.explanation: Stiffness from prolonged immobilisation and oedema is the commonest complication; others include malunion, EPL rupture and Sudeck's atrophy (complex regional pain syndrome).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient develops a swollen, shiny, painful hand with stiffness four weeks after plaster removal for a wrist fracture. The most likely diagnosis is:

options.D: Complex regional pain syndrome (reflex sympathetic dystrophy)

questions.explanation: Pain out of proportion, swelling, trophic skin changes and stiffness after immobilisation define CRPS type I; early mobilisation, desensitisation and mirror therapy are used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Avascular necrosis after a scaphoid fracture is most likely to affect the:
questions.explanation: The scaphoid blood supply enters distally and runs retrograde, so a waist or proximal pole fracture can leave the proximal fragment avascular.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after a fall on the outstretched hand suggests a fracture of the:
questions.explanation: The scaphoid forms the floor of the anatomical snuffbox. Initial X-rays may be normal, so scaphoid precautions and repeat imaging are used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Myositis ossificans traumatica is most commonly associated with injury around which joint?
questions.explanation: Elbow dislocation or supracondylar fracture treated with vigorous passive stretching can cause heterotopic ossification in the brachialis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the acute stage of myositis ossificans, treatment should include:

options.A: Rest/immobilisation, avoiding massage and forced passive stretching

questions.explanation: Forced stretching and massage aggravate bleeding and bone formation. Active pain-free movement is introduced only after the acute phase subsides.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Dupuytren's contracture is a fibrosis of the:
questions.explanation: Progressive thickening of the palmar aponeurosis creates nodules and cords, flexing the ring and little fingers at the MCP and PIP joints first.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A mallet finger results from rupture or avulsion of the:

options.B: Central slip at the PIP joint
options.C: Extensor tendon at its insertion on the distal phalanx
options.D: Collateral ligament of the MCP joint

questions.explanation: Loss of terminal extensor insertion leaves the DIP joint flexed and unable to extend actively. Treated by splinting the DIP in extension for about 6–8 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a boutonnière deformity of the finger the typical posture is:

options.D: Ulnar deviation at the MCP only

questions.explanation: Central slip rupture lets the lateral bands slip volar to the PIP axis: PIP flexes and DIP hyperextends. A swan-neck is the reverse (PIP hyperextension, DIP flexion).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A swan-neck deformity of the finger consists of:
questions.explanation: Common in rheumatoid arthritis; volar plate laxity at the PIP joint and tight intrinsics produce PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: De Quervain's tenosynovitis involves the tendons of:

options.A: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
options.B: Flexor pollicis longus and flexor carpi radialis
options.C: Extensor carpi ulnaris and extensor digiti minimi
options.D: Extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis

questions.explanation: The first dorsal compartment is inflamed; Finkelstein's test (ulnar deviation with thumb flexed in palm) reproduces pain over the radial styloid.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The carpal tunnel contains the median nerve and:

options.C: Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus tendons

questions.explanation: Nine tendons plus the median nerve pass beneath the flexor retinaculum. Ulnar nerve and artery pass in Guyon's canal.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by compression of the:

options.A: Radial nerve at the spiral groove

questions.explanation: Compression beneath the flexor retinaculum produces night pain and tingling in the thumb, index, middle and radial half of the ring finger; thenar wasting is late.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Tardy ulnar nerve palsy typically follows an old fracture of the:

options.A: Lateral humeral condyle with cubitus valgus
options.B: Medial humeral condyle with cubitus varus

questions.explanation: Progressive cubitus valgus after a lateral condyle non-union stretches the ulnar nerve in the cubital tunnel, causing delayed numbness and weakness years later.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Claw hand (main en griffe) is characteristic of an:
questions.explanation: Paralysed ulnar-supplied lumbricals/interossei leave the ring and little finger MCP hyperextended with IP flexion; the deformity is worse in a low lesion because FDP is intact.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: ‘Pointing index’ (inability to flex the index finger when making a fist) indicates a lesion of the:

options.B: Median nerve (anterior interosseous branch) or median nerve at the wrist/forearm

questions.explanation: Median nerve paralyses FDS and the lateral half of FDP, so the index (and middle) finger remain extended when making a fist.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most common cause of wrist drop is injury to the:

options.C: Radial nerve in the spiral groove (e.g. humeral shaft fracture)
options.D: Median nerve at the carpal tunnel

questions.explanation: Radial nerve palsy leaves the wrist and finger extensors paralysed; a cock-up splint maintains the wrist in extension.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: ‘Saturday night palsy’ is usually which type of nerve injury?
questions.explanation: Compression of the radial nerve against the humerus (e.g. falling asleep with the arm over a chair) causes a conduction block that recovers spontaneously in weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In axonotmesis the nerve injury is characterised by:

options.B: Complete transection of the nerve trunk
options.C: Transient conduction block with no Wallerian degeneration
options.D: Axon and myelin damage with an intact endoneurial tube, allowing recovery at about 1 mm per day

questions.explanation: Seddon: neurapraxia (block only), axonotmesis (axon disruption, connective tissue intact), neurotmesis (complete disruption). Regeneration proceeds at ~1 mm/day or 1 inch per month in axonotmesis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Erb's palsy results from injury to the:

options.C: Upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)

questions.explanation: Upper trunk injury (birth traction injury) produces the ‘waiter's tip’ posture: arm adducted, medially rotated, elbow extended and forearm pronated.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Klumpke's paralysis involves the:

options.D: Lower trunk (C8–T1), causing paralysis of the intrinsic hand muscles

questions.explanation: Klumpke's palsy affects C8–T1: claw hand with possible Horner's syndrome if T1 sympathetic fibres are involved.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The nerve most commonly injured in an anterior dislocation of the shoulder is the:
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus; test sensation over the ‘regimental badge’ area and deltoid contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A Bankart lesion is:

options.A: A compression defect of the posterolateral humeral head
options.B: Avulsion of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum with the capsule
options.D: A tear of the long head of biceps

questions.explanation: Anterior dislocation avulses the anteroinferior labrum (Bankart); the humeral head impacts to cause a Hill–Sachs defect posterolaterally.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Hill–Sachs lesion occurs on the:

options.A: Anteromedial aspect of the humeral head
options.C: Posterolateral aspect of the humeral head

questions.explanation: It is an impaction fracture of the posterolateral humeral head against the anterior glenoid rim during anterior dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The apprehension test for anterior shoulder instability is performed by moving the arm into:
questions.explanation: Abduction with external rotation stresses the anterior capsule; the patient shows apprehension that the shoulder will dislocate.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In shoulder impingement syndrome, the tendon most commonly compressed under the acromion is that of:
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus tendon and subacromial bursa are pinched between the humeral head and coracoacromial arch during abduction/flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In supraspinatus tendinitis the typical painful arc during active abduction is:
questions.explanation: Pain between roughly 60° and 120° of abduction occurs as the tuberosity passes under the acromion; pain at the end of range suggests acromioclavicular pathology.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of limitation of the glenohumeral joint is:
questions.explanation: Cyriax: capsular pattern at the shoulder = greatest loss of lateral rotation, then abduction, then medial rotation, as in adhesive capsulitis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To increase lateral rotation of the glenohumeral joint, the humeral head should be mobilised with:
questions.explanation: Convex–concave rule: humeral head (convex) on glenoid (concave); the head glides in the direction opposite to the bone motion. Lateral rotation needs anterior glide; medial rotation needs posterior glide.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A rotator cuff tear is LEAST likely in:

options.A: A patient younger than 40 years with no trauma
options.B: A patient with weakness of external rotation
options.C: A patient over 60 with night pain
options.D: A patient with an altered scapulohumeral rhythm

questions.explanation: Rotator cuff tears are typically degenerative in older patients; in young patients they follow significant trauma.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which test is most useful for bicipital tendinitis?
questions.explanation: Yergason's: resisted supination with the elbow flexed to 90° elicits pain in the bicipital groove. Speed's test is also used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A grade I acromioclavicular sprain presents with:

options.B: Gross upward displacement of the clavicle
options.C: Complete rupture of the coracoclavicular ligaments
options.D: Local tenderness and mild pain, with no visible deformity and normal stability

questions.explanation: Grade I: AC ligament sprain only. Grade II: AC torn, CC sprained. Grade III: both torn with visible step deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Lachman test for ACL integrity is performed with the knee flexed approximately:
questions.explanation: The Lachman test is the most sensitive for acute ACL tear; it uses 20–30° of flexion with anterior tibial translation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A footballer twists his knee, hears a pop and develops immediate swelling within hours. The most likely injured structure is the:
questions.explanation: Rapid haemarthrosis after a twisting injury strongly suggests an ACL tear; meniscal injuries produce delayed effusion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The classical mechanism of posterior cruciate ligament injury is:

options.A: A valgus force with the foot fixed
options.C: A posteriorly directed force on the proximal tibia (e.g. dashboard injury) with the knee flexed

questions.explanation: Falling on the flexed knee or a dashboard impact drives the tibia backwards, rupturing the PCL; posterior sag sign and posterior drawer are positive.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: McMurray's test is used to detect:
questions.explanation: The knee is flexed, tibia rotated and then extended while palpating the joint line; a click or pain indicates a meniscal lesion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The medial meniscus is injured more commonly than the lateral meniscus because it is:

options.B: Less mobile, being attached to the medial collateral ligament and joint capsule

questions.explanation: The medial meniscus is firmly attached to the deep MCL and capsule, so it is less able to move away from compression and rotation forces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which feature is LEAST associated with an acute medial meniscus tear?
questions.explanation: Quadriceps wasting (especially vastus medialis) occurs with meniscal and other knee injuries; hamstring atrophy is not typical.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The ‘unhappy triad’ of the knee (O'Donoghue) consists of injury to the ACL, MCL and:
questions.explanation: Classically ACL + MCL + medial meniscus (many modern series show the lateral meniscus is more often torn with acute ACL injury).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A dynamic factor contributing to abnormal patellar tracking is:
questions.explanation: Muscle imbalance (weak VMO relative to tight lateral structures) is a dynamic factor; bony shape factors such as a shallow groove are static.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A 15-year-old active boy has pain and a prominent tibial tubercle for 4 months with no systemic illness. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle from repeated quadriceps pull; self-limiting, treated with activity modification and stretching.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The carrying angle at the elbow is decreased (arm adducted more) in:
questions.explanation: Cubitus varus (‘gunstock deformity’) results from malunion of a supracondylar fracture, reducing the carrying angle.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Perthes' disease is:

options.A: Slipped upper femoral epiphysis in an adolescent
options.D: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in a child (4–10 years)

questions.explanation: Legg–Calvé–Perthes disease presents with a painful limp and limited abduction/internal rotation in a young child.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Slipped upper femoral epiphysis typically presents in:

options.A: An obese adolescent boy with hip or referred knee pain

questions.explanation: SUFE occurs at puberty, often overweight; the leg lies externally rotated and shortened. Always examine the hip when a teenager complains of knee pain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Barlow's provocative test and Ortolani's test are used to detect:

options.A: Developmental dysplasia (instability) of the hip in infants

questions.explanation: Ortolani reduces a dislocated hip with a ‘clunk’ (abduct and lift); Barlow dislocates an unstable hip (adduct and push).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Developmental dysplasia of the hip is more common in:

options.B: Firstborn girls with breech presentation and a family history

questions.explanation: Risk factors: female sex, breech, family history, firstborn, oligohydramnios, swaddling with hips extended.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The commonest dislocation of the hip is:

options.A: Anterior, with the limb externally rotated
options.C: Posterior, in a dashboard injury (hip flexed, adducted, internally rotated)

questions.explanation: Posterior dislocation accounts for ~90%; the limb is shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated; sciatic nerve injury is a recognised complication.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive Trendelenburg sign indicates weakness of the:

options.C: Hip abductors (gluteus medius and minimus) on the stance side

questions.explanation: When standing on the weak leg the pelvis drops on the opposite (swing) side. Causes include superior gluteal nerve injury, hip dislocation or coxa vara.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The typical position of the hip in advanced osteoarthritis is:
questions.explanation: OA of the hip produces a capsular pattern (flexion, abduction and medial rotation lost) with a fixed deformity in flexion, adduction and external rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: After a posterolateral approach total hip replacement the patient should be advised to AVOID:

options.A: Hip flexion beyond 90°, adduction past the midline and internal rotation
options.D: Sleeping with a pillow between the knees

questions.explanation: Posterior approach precautions prevent dislocation: no flexion >90°, no crossing legs, no internal rotation. Use raised chairs/toilet seats and a pillow between the legs.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which advice following total hip replacement is INCORRECT?

options.A: Keep a pillow between your legs while sleeping
options.C: When turning, pivot on the operated leg

questions.explanation: Pivoting on the operated leg combines rotation and adduction with the foot fixed and risks dislocation. Patients should take small steps to turn.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A realistic range of knee flexion at discharge after an uncomplicated total knee replacement is about:
questions.explanation: Goals: full extension and at least 90° flexion by discharge, with ongoing improvement to 110–120° in subsequent weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which exercise is most appropriate on the first day after a total knee replacement?
questions.explanation: Early isometric quadriceps work, ankle pumps (DVT prevention), and CPM/active-assisted flexion begin immediately within pain limits.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) the foot is held in:

options.A: Plantar flexion, inversion and forefoot adduction

questions.explanation: CTEV: equinus (plantar flexion) of the hindfoot, varus (inversion) of the heel and adduction of the forefoot, with a cavus arch (CAVE).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In correcting clubfoot by the Ponseti serial casting method, the deformity corrected FIRST is the:
questions.explanation: CAVE order: Cavus, Adductus, Varus, then Equinus last (often with a percutaneous Achilles tenotomy).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most common mechanism of injury to the anterior talofibular ligament is:
questions.explanation: ATFL is the first lateral ligament to tear in a plantar-flexed, inverted ankle. The calcaneofibular ligament is injured next.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The talar tilt (inversion stress) test assesses the integrity of the:
questions.explanation: The anterior drawer test examines ATFL; the talar tilt (inversion) tests the CFL. Eversion stress tests the deltoid.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive Thompson (Simmonds) test, with no plantar flexion on squeezing the calf, indicates:

options.D: A complete rupture of the Achilles tendon

questions.explanation: Squeezing the calf normally produces plantar flexion; absence indicates a ruptured Achilles tendon, often with a palpable gap.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pronation of the foot is a combination of:
questions.explanation: Pronation = eversion + abduction + dorsiflexion; supination = inversion + adduction + plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Cobb's angle is used to measure:

options.B: The magnitude of scoliosis on X-ray

questions.explanation: Lines are drawn along the upper end-plate of the top vertebra and the lower end-plate of the bottom vertebra of the curve; the angle between perpendiculars is the Cobb angle.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most common type of scoliosis seen in adolescents is:
questions.explanation: About 80% of structural scoliosis is idiopathic; adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is more common in girls.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A 14-year-old girl has a 25° thoracic scoliosis. The appropriate initial management is:

options.B: Observation or bracing with exercises, not surgery

questions.explanation: Curves < 25° are observed; 25–45° in a growing child are braced (Boston/Milwaukee); > 45–50° may need surgery.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Milwaukee brace is used in:
questions.explanation: The Milwaukee brace is a cervico-thoraco-lumbo-sacral orthosis used for high thoracic curves in scoliosis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Paraplegia in spinal tuberculosis is most common when the disease is in the:
questions.explanation: The thoracic canal is narrowest relative to the cord and a kyphotic angulation easily compresses it; early signs include flexor spasms and exaggerated reflexes.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Ankylosing spondylitis is strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: HLA-B27 is positive in ~90% of patients. It starts in the sacroiliac joints and ascends, giving the ‘bamboo spine’ on X-ray.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Back pain that IMPROVES with exercise and worsens with rest, with morning stiffness over 30 minutes in a young male, suggests:
questions.explanation: Inflammatory back pain: onset before 40 years, insidious, morning stiffness, improves with exercise, nocturnal pain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Rheumatoid arthritis is most strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: HLA-DR4 (and DR1) carries risk for seropositive rheumatoid arthritis; HLA-B27 is for seronegative spondyloarthropathies.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The earliest visible change in osteoarthritic cartilage is:

options.C: Fibrillation (surface irregularity) of the articular cartilage

questions.explanation: Early OA: loss of proteoglycan and surface fibrillation, followed by cartilage thinning, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes and cysts.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which is NOT a radiological feature of osteoarthritis?
questions.explanation: OA features: narrowing of joint space, osteophytes, sclerosis, cysts. Widening is not a feature.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In long-standing rheumatoid arthritis of the hand, the fingers typically show:

options.B: Ulnar deviation at the metacarpophalangeal joints

questions.explanation: Synovitis stretches the radial collateral structures and extensor tendons subluxe ulnarward. Heberden's nodes are of osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The crystals seen in gouty arthritis are:
questions.explanation: Gout: needle-shaped, negatively birefringent urate crystals; pseudogout: rhomboid, positively birefringent CPPD crystals with chondrocalcinosis (menisci).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Calcification of the menisci (chondrocalcinosis) is a feature of:
questions.explanation: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate deposition typically affects large joints (knee, wrist) in older people.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A neuropathic (Charcot) joint is typically:

options.A: Associated with severe pain at rest

questions.explanation: Loss of pain/proprioception leads to repeated trauma; most common cause is diabetes (foot/ankle); also syphilis, syringomyelia, leprosy.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A greenstick fracture occurs most commonly in:
questions.explanation: Immature bone is more flexible; it bends and cracks on one side while the other cortex stays intact.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The pathognomonic (definite) sign of a fracture is:
questions.explanation: Pain, swelling and tenderness are common but non-specific. Crepitus and abnormal mobility are definitive but should not be deliberately elicited.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Both bones of the forearm in an adult are best immobilised in:
questions.explanation: Neutral rotation keeps the interosseous membrane tensioned and balances pronator and supinator forces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most common bone fractured during birth (birth injury) is the:
questions.explanation: Clavicle fracture occurs in difficult deliveries (shoulder dystocia) and heals well with minimal treatment.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A stress (fatigue) fracture is most common in the:

options.A: Metatarsals, tibia and neck of femur

questions.explanation: Repetitive loading, e.g. in runners and military recruits, produces fatigue fractures of the second/third metatarsal, tibia and femoral neck.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Prolonged immobilisation commonly results in all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Immobility causes disuse osteopenia, contracture, hypercalciuria with stones, pressure sores and DVT; gallstones are not an effect.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The maximum weight which can safely be used with skin traction is about:
questions.explanation: Skin traction relies on adhesive or non-adhesive bandages and cannot withstand more than about 4–5 kg without skin damage; skeletal traction is used for heavier forces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most reliable early clinical sign of compartment syndrome is:

options.C: Pain out of proportion to the injury, worsened by passive stretch of the muscles in the compartment

questions.explanation: Pain on passive stretch is the earliest sign. Pulselessness, pallor and paralysis are late; diagnosis is clinical, with pressure measurement when uncertain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When bandaging a transfemoral residual limb, the bandage should:

options.A: Be applied only horizontally across the limb
options.B: Apply greater pressure distally than proximally using diagonal turns, without wrinkles
options.C: Avoid including the hip joint in a figure-of-eight
options.D: Apply more pressure proximally than distally

questions.explanation: Distal pressure shapes the limb and reduces oedema; proximal tourniquet effect must be avoided. Wrinkles and circular constriction cause pressure sores.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Prone lying for 30 minutes several times a day is of particular importance after which amputation?
questions.explanation: Prone lying stretches the hip flexors and helps prevent hip flexion contracture, which would prevent a good prosthetic gait.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a patellar tendon-bearing (PTB) transtibial prosthesis the main weight-bearing areas are the:

options.A: Patellar tendon and pressure-tolerant areas such as the medial tibial flare
options.B: Head of the fibula and tibial crest
options.D: Distal end of the residual limb

questions.explanation: The PTB socket is relieved over the tibial crest, fibular head and distal end (pressure-intolerant) and loads the patellar tendon and medial tibial flare.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: According to the rule of nines, the percentage of total body surface area of ONE adult lower limb is:
questions.explanation: Adult: head 9, each arm 9, chest 18, back 18, each leg 18, perineum 1. A child has a proportionally larger head.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A burn destroying the entire epidermis and dermis with damage to subcutaneous tissue is classified as:
questions.explanation: Full-thickness burns are painless, leathery and need grafting.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A full-thickness burn over the anterior neck is most likely to lead to a contracture in:
questions.explanation: Anterior neck scar shortens and pulls the neck into flexion; therapists must position the neck in extension without a pillow and use splints/collars.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
